 ::JUDGMENT:
:
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 SCCH-5 for the relief of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
2.

The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 04.06.2022 at about 7.15 p.m. petitioner was riding a Passion Pro motor cycle bearing Reg. No. AP-03-CT-3604 along with a pillion rider on Service Road, near Chinnuru Flyover, Gangavaram Mandal, Chitoor District, Andhra Pradesh, at that time, a Tata Nexon Car bearing Reg. No.AP-39-MA-5842 being driven by its driver from behind at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle, as a result of which, he fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Palamaner and after firstaid he was shifted Shri Sai Jagadish Hospital,
Tirupathi, thereafter shifted to Suraksha Hospitals, Tirupathi, SCCH-5 wherein he took treatment as inpatient and towards the hospitalization charges, medicines, conveyance charges he has spent a sum of Rs.3,50,000/-.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 46 years, hale and healthy, working as agriculturist, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is permanently disabled, unable to do daily activities, he has also lost his earnings.
With regard to accident crime No.115/2022 is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle before the Gangavaram Police for the offences punishable under Sec.337, 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
SCCH-5 4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has not appeared before court hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
Further submitted that, vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-CT-3604 was duly insured with respondent No.2 and liability if limited to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further respondent No.2 submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any Indu Kumar M vs Manoj Kumar N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115558519/
2 basis.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.159 of M.V.Act and driver of the car was not having any valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5.

Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
SCCH-5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 04.06.2022 at about 7.15 p.m. near Service Road,
Chinnuru Flyover, Gangavaram Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh due to rash and negligent driving of Tata Nexon Car bearing Reg. No.AP-39-MA-5842 dashed against the petitioner motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Dr.Jagadish Muppalam, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sri Sai Jagadish Hospital as PW-2 and marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.
SCCH-5 7.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :

As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8.
Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint and translated copy of complaint as Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.2A, copy of sketch and translated copy of SCCH-5 sketch as Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.3A, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.5.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal Indu Kumar M vs Manoj Kumar N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115558519/
3 of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 04.06.2022 and injuries sustained by the petitioner as alleged in the petition.

sentences.text: 10. Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and to discard the evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 04.06.2022 at about SCCH-5 7.15 p.m. while he was riding Passion Pro motor cycle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-CT-3604 on Service Road,
near Chinnuru Flyover, Gangavaram Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh.
11. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the Tata Nexon Car bearing Reg. No.AP-39-MA-5842.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained Type 1 compound bimalleolar fracture left ankle (lower end of left fibula fracture), puncture wound on left leg and other injuries all over the body and for the said injuries he underwent SCCH-5 left fibula plating +
mediamallelous CC screw fixation.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.4, initial statement receipt marked as Ex.P.6, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Suraksha Hospitals, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient from 05.06.2022 to 07.06.2022.

Further he has exhibited medical bills for Rs.63,249/- marked as Ex.P.10 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.11.
13.
Further Dr.Jagadish Muppalam is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited case sheet as Ex.P.12, recent examination report as Ex.P.13 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.14 and he has assessed permanent disability of 26% of left lower limb, which is 13% of whole body.

In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not personally treated the petitioner and further deposed that, at the time of SCCH-5 treating the petitioner, he was in normal condition and after discharge, the petitioner has continued follow up treatment.

Further deposed that,
fractures are united. PW-2 deposed that, petitioner can do light work and cannot do hard work and incase the implant is removed, the complaints of petitioner may reduce.
Further deposed that, he has only assessed physical disability.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 5% for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

14. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 46 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.9, wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner as 1978 and the alleged accident is occurred in the year 2022, SCCH-5 accordingly relying on Ex.P.10 his age is 44 years as on the date of accident,but on perusal of the wound certificate and discharge summary, age of the petitioner is mentioned as 45 years and 43 years respectively,
accordingly relying on above records, age of the petitioner is considered as 45 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 14 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Indu Kumar M vs Manoj Kumar N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115558519/
4

15. As per his case, he was working as agriculturist, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of SCCH-5 Rs.15,500/- p.m. so that,
said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 05.06.2022 to 07.06.2022 i.e., for 2 days.

As per the evidence of PW-2 he examined petitioner on 18.03.2025 i.e., nearly after 3 years on occurrence of the accident and on examination date as per version of PW-2 and by considering the gravity of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least three months to heal the wound.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of SCCH-5 income.

As per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e.,
Rs.15,500/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.

So petitioner is entitled for Rs.46,500/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
17.
Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.10 medical bills for Rs.63,249/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.4 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 04.06.2022.
So as per Ex.P.4 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained lower end of left SCCH-5 fibula fracture, which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against N. Manoj Kumar for the offences punishable under Sec.337, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
18.
Per contra except denial in the written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to proved the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondent No.2 has filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case.
SCCH-5 19.
Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

21. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.201150010521800048300 which is valid for the SCCH-5 period from 15.01.2022 to 14.01.2025,
the alleged accident was occurred on 04.06.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident,
insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

22. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,94,949/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Ninety Four Thousand Nine Hundred Forty Nine Only) with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
